title: Olive's Sound Game
note: b385 — first use of 'acorn', 'petal_single' and 'scratch_mark'. P2/p3's decorative border of small 'p'/'n' objects is simplified to one or two small-scale props per corner rather than a literal three-item border each time — a dedicated generic 'nose' icon and a 'nettle' prop were judged not worth inventing for a single page each; p3 reuses the small 'bush' prop in the nettle's spot. P4's 'thread of light stretching between' the two acorns is omitted (no thread/line prop exists for it) — the two acorns held apart still carry the scene.

pages.brief: Olive the plum owl perched importantly on a low branch, one wing extended like a teacher, big amber eyes fixed on the reader. Two smaller birds sitting below her on the grass, attentive. Autumn oak leaves framing the page.
pages.alt: Olive the owl perches importantly on a low branch, one wing extended like a teacher, while Pip and Ned sit attentively on the grass below her.

pages.brief: Pip standing tall and proud on a stone, chest puffed out. Around him, drawn small like a border, a pond, a flower pot and a single petal. Sand-and-gold palette to match Pip.
pages.alt: Pip stands tall and proud on a stone, chest puffed out, with a small pond, a flower pot and a single petal drawn around him like a border.

pages.brief: Ned the duckling going cross-eyed trying to look at his own beak, one webbed foot lifted. A nest, a nose and a nettle drawn around him in the same border style as the previous page. Funny.
pages.alt: Ned the duckling goes cross-eyed trying to look at his own beak, one webbed foot lifted, with a small nest and a bush drawn around him in a border.

pages.brief: Olive holding one acorn in each foot and slowly pulling them apart, with a thread of light stretching between them. Pip and Ned lean in, wings and flippers out ready. Slightly magical.
pages.alt: Olive holds one acorn in each foot, slowly pulling them apart, while Pip and Ned lean in close, ready, in a slightly magical moment.

pages.brief: Three separate acorn-shapes floating apart across the page, and behind them, only faintly visible, a warm round sun beginning to show through. Do not draw the sun fully yet.
pages.alt: Three separate acorn shapes float apart across the page, with a warm round sun only faintly visible beginning to show through behind them.

pages.brief: Four pieces of twig floating apart in a curve; behind them the faint outline of Pip's ivy nest starting to assemble itself. Same visual logic as the previous page so children spot the pattern.
pages.alt: Four pieces of twig float apart in a curve, with the faint outline of a nest beginning to assemble itself behind them.

pages.brief: Pip tumbling backwards off the branch with his legs in the air and an expression of total astonishment, feathers everywhere. Ned laughing. Olive entirely unbothered, still holding her acorns. Full-page, energetic, the funniest picture in the book.
pages.alt: Pip tumbles backwards off the branch with his legs in the air and total astonishment on his face, feathers everywhere, while Ned laughs and Olive sits entirely unbothered, still holding her acorns.

pages.brief: Closing page. Olive scratching a single shape into a patch of bare earth with one claw — deliberately just a mark, not a readable letter. The three of them looking down at it together in the last of the light. Quiet, expectant.
pages.alt: Olive scratches a single simple mark into the bare earth with one claw — just a mark, not a letter — while Pip and Ned look down at it together in the last quiet light of the day.
